SCHOOL ROOM · THE CLUBS · 45 CARDS · AGES 3–12

The Clubs — every card opens a hobby.

Forty-five after-school clubs on forty-five cards: art, music, dance and thirteen more for the youngest members, then chess, coding, fencing and the rest for ages 6 and up. Every card prints the two skills its club trains — Aim & Focus, Calm & Wellbeing, Measure & Create — every club has its lesson and printable twin right here, and the room was built for choosing: try one, keep one, grow one.

Open the club shelves ↓The printable set ↗
HOW THIS ROOM WORKS

Pick a club. Read its skills. Try it this week.

Every card in this deck does two jobs: it names one club and it prints the two skills that club trains, right under the picture. The room splits by age the way the school does: the first shelf holds the fifteen clubs made for the youngest members — tagged Ages 3+ — and the second shelf holds the thirty clubs for older members, tagged Ages 6+. When one club becomes a favorite, its lesson page carries the full teaching — what the club is, what the skills secretly train, the parent script, the questions to ask — and the library page holds the printable twin with a download button.

A word on safety, because it matters here: some clubs are coach clubs. Fencing and archery always run with a trained coach and proper equipment — their pages say so — and swimming, climbing and horse riding belong wherever trained adults and the right gear are standard. The card starts the hobby; the grown-ups keep it safe.

THE YOUNG CLUB SHELF · AGES 3+

Fifteen clubs for the youngest members.

Art, music, dance, sports, drama, gardening, cooking, ballet, yoga, swimming, reading, crafts, drawing, baking and singing — the fifteen clubs that work from age three, in the order the school recommends trying them. Read every card right here on this page.

ArtMusicDanceSportsDramaGardeningCookingBalletYogaSwimmingReadingCraftsDrawingBakingSinging
THE OLDER CLUB SHELF · AGES 6+

Thirty clubs for ages 6 and up.

From archery to volunteering — the strategy clubs, the workshop clubs, the coach-led sports and the word clubs. Younger members wait for these; the skills are worth the wait.

GAMES THE CLUBS PLAY

Warm-ups from the games shelf.

Club time and game time trade places all afternoon, and the school’s games shelf holds the rules for the warm-ups every club borrows: Animal Walks opens dance, drama and yoga bodies, Musical Statues trains the freeze every performance needs, Relay Race is sports club’s favorite drill, Obstacle Course is gymnastics night at home, and Simon Says sharpens the listening every club runs on. Full rules on every page.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where to wander next.

Explore the School — every room, one door each ↗The Growing-up classrooms on the Learning Path ↗Visit the Art Studio · ages 3–12 ↗Run an experiment in the Science Lab ↗Go outside with the Nature Club ↗

The Clubs sit on the school’s room shelf beside the Library, the Garden, the Playground, the Music Room and the Art Room — and they belong to the Growing-up classrooms the Learning Path points to: the Art Studio, the Science Lab and the Nature Club are the neighbors a new hobby grows into.

A hobby is a curriculum. Every card here hides real work — focus, patience, practice, courage — inside something the child thinks is just their club. Try the thing first; the skills follow the fun.

TEACHER’S LESSON

How this class is taught.

By the end of this class: your child has met all 45 cards in Extra-Curricular Activities, said each word with you and tried one small activity from the lesson.

  1. 01
    Welcome

    “Hello! Today we are learning about Extra-Curricular Activities. We have 45 cards, and we will look at them one at a time.”

    How: Sit side by side with the cards in front of you. Keep your voice warm and unhurried, and let your child touch the cards.

  2. Cards 1–10
  3. 02
    Card 1 · Art

    “Art club! Today we paint — any color, any idea. Painting & Creativity means there is no wrong picture. What will yours be?”

    How: Tape three papers side by side and paint one thing across all three — a caterpillar, a rainbow, a long road. A painting that keeps going past the edge feels wonderfully rule-breaking.

  4. 03
    Card 2 · Music

    “Music club! Let’s find the beat — clap with me: one, two, one, two. Rhythm & Sound is the club’s secret pair. What sound can your hands make?”

    How: Play echo claps: you clap a short pattern, the child claps it back, then swap. Two rounds in, let the child lead the pattern — leaders never want the game to end.

  5. 04
    Card 3 · Dance

    “Dance club! Put a song on and let your body listen. Movement & Expression — your arms can say happy, your knees can say silly. Show me!”

    How: Freeze dance: dance while the song plays, freeze when it stops — and hold the freeze like a statue with a secret. Three songs later, everyone is warm and laughing.

  6. 05
    Card 4 · Sports

    “Sports club! Today we move as a team — roll the ball to me, I roll it back. Teamwork & Fitness: the ball travels, our legs travel, everybody wins.”

    How: Set up a two-goal living-room soccer game with a soft ball and chair goals. Keep score out loud, shake hands after — the handshake is the real sport.

  7. 06
    Card 5 · Drama

    “Drama club! Pick a character — a dragon, a dentist, a detective. Stories & Confidence means the story is yours. How does your character walk?”

    How: Play story suitcase: grab three random objects and invent the story that connects them — the spoon, the shoe and the teddy bear were all on the same picnic.

  8. 07
    Card 6 · Gardening

    “Gardening club! We plant the seed, we water it, and then we wait. Nature & Care — gardens teach waiting better than anyone. Where should our pot live?”

    How: Plant a bean in a clear cup against the side so the root is visible. Water it, name it, and check it every morning — first sprouts arrive in about a week.

  9. 08
    Card 7 · Cooking

    “Cooking club! Today you are the chef — I am the helper. Food & Independence means you make the choices: stir, pour, taste. What do we cook first?”

    How: Build-your-own faces: a rice cake, spread, and fruit pieces for eyes, noses and silly smiles. The chef assembles, the chef eats, the chef is extremely proud.

  10. 09
    Card 8 · Ballet

    “Ballet club! Arms round like a bubble, heels together — first position. Balance & Grace: dancers are strong AND gentle. Can you stand like a dancer?”

    How: Practice the tiptoe walk across the hallway — a plate of pretend hot soup balanced on one hand, slow steps, no spills. Ballet is secretly balance training in disguise.

  11. 10
    Card 9 · Yoga

    “Yoga club! Feet down like roots, hands together up high — tree pose. Calm & Wellbeing: yoga is how bodies say ahh. How long can you hold it?”

    How: Animal breaths: snake hiss (long and slow), lion roar (big exhale), bunny sniffs (three quick ones). Breathing becomes a game the body asks for at bedtime.

  12. 11
    Card 10 · Swimming

    “Swimming club! Water has rules and we know them: never alone, always a grown-up watching. Confidence & Safety — brave AND careful. Ready to blow bubbles?”

    How: Practice pool rules on dry land: walk by the pool (never run), enter feet first, and the grown-up-on-the-step game — swim TO someone, not AWAY from everyone.

  13. Cards 11–20
  14. 12
    Card 11 · Reading

    “Reading club! Pick the book, pick the spot — your lap is the library today. Imagine & Learn: books are movies for your brain. Which page should we stop on to guess?”

    How: Read a page, then each person predicts what happens next — closest guess picks the next book. Prediction turns listening into a sport.

  15. 13
    Card 12 · Crafts

    “Crafts club! Grab the box — tubes, paper, stickers, string. Make & Explore: we build the thing, then we build a better thing. What should today’s creature be?”

    How: The tube zoo challenge: five cardboard tubes, five animals, one shelf for the grand opening. Every zookeeper names their animals — names are the finishing touch.

  16. 14
    Card 13 · Drawing

    “Drawing club! First we look, then we draw — look at the apple: round, with a little stem. See & Create: artists copy the world and invent their own. What do we draw first?”

    How: Blind-contour game: draw your own hand WITHOUT looking at the paper, eyes on your fingers the whole time. The result looks hilarious — and teaches more than any neat drawing.

  17. 15
    Card 14 · Baking

    “Baking club! Baking is a recipe-follower’s game: one cup, two teaspoons, level it off. Measure & Create — careful measuring makes the magic. Ready to pour?”

    How: Muffin math: let the child measure and pour every ingredient, counting each scoop out loud. Half the learning is in the measuring; the other half is warm from the oven.

  18. 16
    Card 15 · Singing

    “Singing club! Everybody has a voice and yours is the only one like it. Voice & Confidence: big breath, big sound, no shy notes. What song lives in you today?”

    How: Sing the echo game: you sing a line, the child echoes it, then swap — and let the child invent a line for YOU to echo. Silly words welcome; confidence doubles.

  19. 17
    Card 16 · Archery

    “Archery club! This one is a with-a-coach sport: real bows live with trained grown-ups. Aim & Focus — archers breathe slow and aim steady. At home we practice the aim; the arrows wait for the range.”

    How: Home aim training, no arrows: toss beanbags at a hoop, roll socks into a laundry-basket bullseye, hold a pose for five slow breaths before every throw. Focus first; bow later.

  20. 18
    Card 17 · Astronomy

    “Astronomy club! Tonight the ceiling is the sky — stars, the moon, a planet or two. Wonder & Discovery: astronomers ask big questions and look, look, look. Find the moon with me.”

    How: Moon diary: draw the moon’s shape every night for two weeks in the same little notebook. Halfway through, the child predicts the next shape — and is usually right.

  21. 19
    Card 18 · Bird Watching

    “Bird watching club! Voices down, eyes up — what flew past? Observe & Discover: watchers look for color, size, song. Our first three birds get names in the notebook.”

    How: Window tally: a paper by the window with three bird drawings. Every visit gets a tally mark. By Friday the family knows exactly who the regulars are.

  22. 20
    Card 19 · Calligraphy

    “Calligraphy club! Slow pens write the prettiest letters — downstrokes thick, upstrokes thin. Letters & Patience: we write ONE letter today and we write it ten times, beautifully.”

    How: Fill one page with a single letter, huge, then tiny, then fancy — a whole family of A’s (or the child’s own initial). Sign the page like an artist signs a print.

  23. 21
    Card 20 · Chess

    “Chess club! Every piece has a job — the knight jumps, the rook runs straight, the king is precious. Focus & Strategy: good players think before they touch. What is your plan?”

    How: Learn pawn chess first: pawns only, first to reach the far side wins. One game teaches how the littlest pieces do the biggest work.

  24. Cards 21–30
  25. 22
    Card 21 · Choir

    “Choir club! Singing alone is a solo; singing together is a choir. Voice & Harmony: listen to your neighbor as much as yourself. Can we hold one long note — together?”

    How: Round singing: one person starts a short song, a second starts the same song two lines later, and the two versions weave. Row Your Boat is the classic first round.

  26. 23
    Card 22 · Climbing

    “Climbing club! Walls are climbed with a plan — hand, hand, foot, foot. Courage & Movement: being brave does not mean rushing. At the gym, the rope team is trained; at home we train grips.”

    How: Home grip and balance work: hang from a playground bar two seconds longer each day, walk a curb like a balance beam, plan three-point contact — always two hands and a foot or two feet and a hand.

  27. 24
    Card 23 · Coding

    “Coding club! Computers follow instructions exactly — even the silly ones. Logic & Discovery: programmers write steps, test, fix, test again. Give ME the instructions: make a sandwich, step by step!”

    How: Robot parent: the child writes or calls out exact steps, and you obey them literally — turn in circles when told circle, walk into the couch when the step was missing. Debugging begins at home.

  28. 25
    Card 24 · Cycling

    “Cycling club! Helmet first, always. Balance & Adventure: eyes up, pedals round, and the bike rides under you. Where should our first ride go — the corner and back?”

    How: Scoot-first learning: take the pedals off a small bike and let the child push with their feet, lifting both feet for glides. Balance arrives on its own; pedals reattach later like a promotion.

  29. 26
    Card 25 · Debate

    “Debate club! Today’s question: are dogs or cats the better pet? Speak & Listen — one voice at a time, everyone heard. Pick your side and give me your first reason.”

    How: Family debate night with a silly question: summer or winter, pancakes or waffles. Two reasons each, then switch sides and argue the OTHER view — empathy with a timer.

  30. 27
    Card 26 · Fencing

    “Fencing club! Fencers salute before every bout — respect first, sword second. Agility & Focus: quick feet, quiet mind. At home we practice footwork; the blades live at the club with the coach.”

    How: Home footwork drills: the advance (step forward), the retreat (step back), the lunge (big step, front knee bent) — five of each, pillow on the head for posture. The coach supplies the sword.

  31. 28
    Card 27 · Fashion Design

    “Fashion design club! Every outfit started as a drawing. Imagine & Create: designers sketch, choose fabric, and build. Design an outfit for rainy days — what should it do besides look great?”

    How: Paper-doll runway: draw and cut three outfits for the same paper figure — rain, party, snow — then hold a runway show and explain each choice out loud.

  32. 29
    Card 28 · Filmmaking

    “Filmmaking club! A film is a story with a camera — opening, middle, THE END. Imagine & Tell: directors plan the shots. Scene one: the dog walks in. Action!”

    How: The one-minute documentary: film how a sandwich is really made, interview the chef, shoot the grand finale bite. Premiere after dinner, audience applauds, credits roll.

  33. 30
    Card 29 · First Aid

    “First aid club! Helpers know three things: check, call, care — check what happened, call a grown-up, keep the hurt person company. Help & Care: brave helpers practice BEFORE the emergency.”

    How: Role-play the drill: a stuffed animal has a scrape. Clean the pretend wound, apply the pretend bandage, say the calming words. Then rehearse the real phone number out loud, twice.

  34. 31
    Card 30 · Gymnastics

    “Gymnastics club! Strong AND stretchy — that is the whole sport. Strength & Flexibility: tuck the chin for a roll, hold the arms for a balance. Show me your strongest still statue.”

    How: The animal warm-up before any rolling: bear walk, crab walk, frog jump, flamingo stand. Two minutes of animals and the body is ready for real skills on a soft surface.

  35. Cards 31–40
  36. 32
    Card 31 · Horse Riding

    “Horse riding club! Horses are big and kind — we move slowly, speak softly, and a grown-up or instructor is always there. Courage & Care: riders are brave AND gentle. Can you hello the horse with a flat hand?”

    How: Pre-riding practice: groom a friend’s dog with a soft brush the way riders groom horses — slow strokes, kind voice. Then practice mounting posture on a chair, back tall, eyes up.

  37. 33
    Card 32 · Journaling

    “Journaling club! This notebook is yours — spelling does not matter, truth does. Reflect & Express: writers write what the day was really like. What was today’s headline?”

    How: Three-lines-a-day rule: today I saw / today I felt / tomorrow I hope. Three lines takes two minutes, and two minutes keeps the habit alive for months.

  38. 34
    Card 33 · Lego

    “Lego club! Bricks first, then a bridge, then a whole city. Build & Create: builders sort, stack, test — and rebuild when the tower leans. What are we building today?”

    How: The rebuild challenge: follow a small set’s instructions once, then take it apart and build something completely new from the same pieces. The second build is where creativity lives.

  39. 35
    Card 34 · Martial Arts

    “Martial arts club! Every class starts with a bow — respect for the teacher, the space and ourselves. Discipline & Strength: martial artists are strong AND calm. Can you stand in ready stance for five breaths?”

    How: Home kata practice: three slow moves — block, punch, block — in front of a mirror, five times slow, five times quick. Slow builds the shape; fast builds the power.

  40. 36
    Card 35 · Nature Crafts

    “Nature crafts club! We take only what has already fallen — leaves, twigs, seed pods. Collect & Create: nature gives the materials, we give the idea. What is that leaf becoming?”

    How: Leaf-and-stick animal gallery: flat leaf = owl body, twig legs, stone head, glue on card. Three animals make a gallery; a gallery needs an opening night with juice.

  41. 37
    Card 36 · Photography

    “Photography club! A photographer asks: what is the most interesting thing right here? Observe & Create: steady hands, one subject, click. What will your first photo be of?”

    How: The five-photo scavenger hunt: something red, something tiny, something that makes you laugh, something from below, something that shows today. Five pictures, one story.

  42. 38
    Card 37 · Poetry

    “Poetry club! Poems are small — five lines can hold a whole feeling. Words & Feelings: poets pick words the way painters pick colors. What does rain sound like to you?”

    How: List poem recipe: I like / I wonder / I remember / I dream / I wish — one line each, and the last line is read with the biggest voice in the house.

  43. 39
    Card 38 · Pottery

    “Pottery club! Clay listens to hands — press slow, turn the lump, press again. Shape & Imagine: potters see the bowl inside the mud. What are we making for the kitchen?”

    How: Pinch-pot start: push a thumb into a ball of clay and pinch the walls thin by turning and squeezing — the oldest pottery trick on Earth, still the first thing students learn.

  44. 40
    Card 39 · Puppetry

    “Puppetry club! The puppet is shy until it has a voice — high, low, growly? Create & Perform: puppeteers build the character, then act. What is your puppet’s name?”

    How: Doorway stage: a sheet hung in a doorway, knees behind it, one puppet at a time peeking over. A two-scene show — hello, joke, goodbye — is a complete first production.

  45. 41
    Card 40 · Robotics

    “Robotics club! A robot is a machine that follows a plan — vacuum robots, factory arms, the Mars rover. Build & Invent: engineers build, test, improve. What job should YOUR robot do?”

    How: Human robot course: one player is the robot (eyes closed or blindfolded), the other gives exact commands — two steps forward, quarter turn left. Reach the teddy bear: mission accomplished.

  46. Cards 41–45
  47. 42
    Card 41 · Science

    “Science club! Scientists write their guess down BEFORE the test — that is what makes it fair. Explore & Experiment: we ask, we try, we look closely. What is our first question?”

    How: Sink-or-float census: fill the sink, gather ten small objects, have everyone vote sink or float before each one lands. Wrong predictions are the best part — they mean a discovery is happening.

  48. 43
    Card 42 · Skateboarding

    “Skateboarding club! Helmet, pads, flat ground — then one gentle push. Balance & Confidence: skaters fall, get up, and fall better. Can you stand on the board while it stands still?”

    How: Carpet first: put the board on a rug and practice stance and weight shifts where it cannot roll. Then grass, then smooth pavement — each surface one notch braver.

  49. 44
    Card 43 · Table Tennis

    “Table tennis club! Little swings — the ball is light, the table is close. React & Play: watch the ball all the way to your paddle. Ready — one bounce on each side, how many can we keep going?”

    How: Cooperative rallies, not competition: count consecutive hits together and try to beat the family record. The record chase makes every player better without a single lost point.

  50. 45
    Card 44 · Tennis

    “Tennis club! Side-on stance, smooth swing — the ball loves a calm racket. Move & Compete: tennis players run AND score with a handshake after. Can you bounce the ball ten times on the racket?”

    How: Racket-control ladder before any serving: ten bounces flat, ten bounces on the racket edge, walk while bouncing, then a partner toss-and-hit over a bench net. The ladder makes the court feel smaller.

  51. 46
    Card 45 · Volunteering

    “Volunteering club! Helpers do not need money — they need time and kind eyes. Share & Support: volunteers see a problem and offer a hand. What can we do for someone this week?”

    How: The two-basket donation: with the child, fill one basket of toys to give away and one box of pantry food for a local drive. The child carries the delivery — carrying it is the moment.

  52. 47
    Practice

    “Now you are the teacher! Pick any card and tell me what it is.”

    How: Let your child choose the card and say the word in their own way. Teaching someone else is the strongest way to remember.

  53. 48
    Check

    “Can you find Art? Now show me Coding.”

    How: A point, a fetch or the word all count as a pass. If they are unsure, name it for them and try again another day — there are no scores and no pressure.

  54. 49
    Well done

    “Well done! Today we met 45 cards. Let us look for one of them at home.”

    How: End on a win, then spot one of the words in real life today. Meeting it again in the real world is what makes it stay.

Read the script while you show the cards — the say-lines are yours to say out loud and the how-lines are the activity behind each step. Skip, shorten or repeat anything: the class bends to your child, never the other way round.
